text: A RAG system can be decomposed into retrieval and generation stage.
The objective of retrieval process is to find contents within the knowledge base that are closely related to the user query, by chunking external knowledge,
creating embeddings, indexing, and similarity search.
Documents are divided into smaller segments, with each segment containing a distinct unit of information.
An embedding model compresses each information chunk into a vector representation.
The user query is also converted into its vector representation through the same vectorization process, so that the user query can be compared
Indexing, this process stores these text chunks and their vector embeddings as key value pairs, enabling efficient and scalable search
For large external knowledge bases that exceed memory capacity, vector databases offer efficient long-term storage.
Similarity scores between the query embeddings and text chunk embeddings are calculated, which are used for searching information highly relevant to the user
The generation process of the RAG system then combines retrieved information with the user query to form the augmented query which is parsed to the LLM to
